paragraphs.content:
Throughout life, we're able to set an intention: focus on breaking complex concepts and ideas into simple, easy-to-digest, bite-sized morsels of mental nutrition.

The Human Needs Concept — no exception to that — is all about looking at why we humans do the things we do...

(( You know those things we do: the interesting, the mundane; the exciting, the boring; the kind, the unkind; the expected, the unexpected; and, sometimes the wildly unpredictable ))

... then, categorizing all of those reasons for doing what we do into six basic, easy-to-understand factors.

And, finally, we can learn how to apply these factors in order to live a happier, healthier, more fulfilling existence for ourselves and our loved ones.

The concept itself is rooted in what legendary Life Coach, speaker, and author, Tony Robbins, conceptualized, coined, and popularized: The 6 Human Needs.

So, why is it that some people act in a way that others may judge or label to be unacceptable, inappropriate, immature, or childish when things don't go their way? Why do some people thrive in solitude, while others seek to constantly be surrounded by others? Why is it that some of us affix ourselves to daily routines and stay close to home, while others of us galavant whimsically around the world?

We'll answer these questions (and, many more) together as we set our sights on unpacking and unraveling The Human Needs Concept.

The power in this is that it's actually quite simple. In fact, nearly all human behavior can be explained by these six factors.

So, grab your popcorn — or fruitbowl, or ice cream, or snack of choice — strap your seatbelt on, and get ready for a wild ride into the human experience!

paragraphs.content: Let's start this off with a bold statement: At the heart of nearly every action, reaction, decision, thought, or emotion lies only a single, definable reason for its existence: one of six fundamental needs either has been or must be satisfied. Boom! 🤯

Sure... at the start, there may seem to be millions of reasons for an action, decision, thought, or feeling.

And, it's absolutely true that there could be ...

But, underneath all of these reasons lies a subset of reasons for these reasons that are much smaller in quantity.

And, those subset reasons for reasons can be grouped into an even smaller subset of reasons for reasons for reasons... 🤪

... and, so on, and so forth.
Think of it like an upside-down pyramid where the many reasons are funnelled down into smaller and smaller collections of reasons until finally, at the core of it all, they hit the point...

And, it's at this point that we will find one (or, more) of 6 factors.

 This is The Human Needs Concept.

topics.topicQuestion: How would it enhance my life if I could simplify every decision to be based on one of only 6 factors?
topics.topicQuestionPrompt: Think of a recent decision I've made and how many reasons I considered in the process...

paragraphs.content: So, what are these six factors that are supposedly at the core of basically everything in human existence? Certainty, Variety, Relevance, Connection, Growing, and Contribution Just in case you have no prior experience with the concept, let's take a quick look at each of these. (And, if you do, here's a little refresher)

Certainty Aka security, aka safety, aka comfort, aka consistency, aka routine, aka predictability At the core of our being lies a primal need for certainty — the stability, safety, and comforts we can sometimes take for granted.

Certainty (cont.) Whether it's consistent income, a steady relationship, the dependable support of family and friends, an exercise routine, or as basic and primal as the assurance of survival, we all seek certainty in our lives in one form or another.

Variety Aka surprises, aka possibility, aka the unknown, aka dreams & aspirations, aka the spice of life, aka change, aka diversity, aka different foods, aka choice. As much as we need predictability and stability, we also crave change and unpredictability.
Variety (cont.) We're creative, we seek adventure, we eat different foods, we watch different shows. The need for diversity in our life can be just as strong as the need for consistency.

Relevance Aka the self, aka uniqueness, aka being the most important person in our lover's, friend's, or family member's life, aka likes / comments / follows, aka achievement, aka praise. And, ohhh boy do we need it! (gender neutral of course)

Relevance (cont.) It's important for each of us that our life means something — no matter what form it takes. And, whether or not we outwardly seek praise or regularly pat ourselves on the back for our achievements, it's important that what we do... matters.

Connection Aka love, aka romance, aka family, aka friends, aka community, aka pets, aka the relationship with yourself Connection between us, with our beloved pets, with ourselves, and even with nature is a fundamental need that transcends cultural, social, and individual boundaries.

Connection (cont.) It goes beyond love — though vitally important in and of itself — and includes belonging to meaningful relationships of any type... ... which, in turn, nutures our emotional well-being.

Growing Aka progress, aka development, aka promotions, aka maturations, aka expansion, aka learning, aka experiencing, aka building skillsets. Whether or not its overplayed, the phrase,"if it's not Growing, it's dying", is a fact of life.

Growing (cont.) Whether we're looking for a promotion or a raise; to be stronger, faster, better; to learn more; to achieve more; to have more; to do more; or, to be more; growing plays a crucial role in human existence. We build, we expand, we seek more... it's who we are.

Contribution Aka giving, aka sharing, aka being a part of something bigger than ourselves, aka teaching, aka coaching, aka making a difference. We all contribute: our work serves our society; we take care of our family and friends; we give gifts on holidays...

Contribution (cont.) ... but, it goes beyond just our personal spheres. We also have an opportunity to contribute to people we don't know, to the greater good, and to the happiness, health, and well-being of the world as a whole.

topics.topicQuestion: Thinking about a challenge I've faced recently, how could a better understanding of my own human needs help me navigate this challenge more effectively?
topics.topicQuestionPrompt: Which need(s) played / plays role? How?

paragraphs.content: As we turn our gaze towards how these needs impact our individual and collective lives, let's also take a quick look at how they interconnect, give birth to countless subsets, and weave the complex web of reasons that shape our lives.

For example, the need for certainty can create a child subset of 'financial security' (when the need is met), 'financial worry' (when the need may not be met), and 'financial burden' (when the need is not met).

And, to help us meet our need for certainty as it relates to finances, we may 'seek a promotion or raise' (Growing), 'take on additional employment' (Variety), or even 'take a loan' (Connection).

Romantic relationships (Connection) provide a prime example for how every need is interconnected:

We seek a stable relationship where we know the other person will be there for us when we need them (Certainty)...

We want to try new things together, go new places together, or even — in some cases — explore other partners (Variety)...

We want to know that we're special and important in the eyes of our partner (Relevance)...

We want to learn more about them — or, at least have them learn more about us and what we like / don't like (Growing)...

And, we want to give and / or be given gifts, attention, time, stuff, etc etc (Contribution)

There's little doubt that each of these needs plays a role in our individual and collective lives.

And, their interplay and interconnectedness — with unlimited combinations — are what create the vast number of decisions, attitudes, personalities, behaviors, moods, actions, and more.
Thinking about your own life, what interconnectness have these needs shown as it relates to your family or household? No doubt, more than one of these needs plays a role for you...
Do you give lots of your time and energy (Contribution)? Do you lead by example (Relevance)? Do you play games, go on trips, try different foods together (Variety)?
How about stability in the household (Certainty)? Do you learn new things together or about each other (Growing)?

As we wrap up this section of the course, it's important for us to note that there's no place for oppressive judgement about how these needs play a role in our life or in the life of someone else.

We're all living our lives and doing what we can with what we know.

The key is to learn where we can improve, where we're doing well, and on what we may want to focus our attention.
